14 नवम्बर यानी Children's Day पर बॉलीवुड एक्ट्रेस सोहा अली खान ने फैंस को एक बेहद खास सरप्राइज दिया है! 📸

सोहा ने अपने Instagram अकाउंट पर अपनी मां शर्मिला टैगोर और पिता मंसूर अली खान पटौदी (टाइगर पटौदी) के बचपन की तीन अनसीन तस्वीरें शेयर की हैं। इन तस्वीरों में दोनों देश के पहले प्रधानमंत्री जवाहरलाल नेहरू के साथ नजर आ रहे हैं। 🌟

एक तस्वीर में नन्हीं शर्मिला नेहरू जी के कोट पर कुछ पिन लगाती दिख रही हैं, तो दूसरी में वो All India Radio (AIR) में उनके पास खड़ी हैं। तीसरी फोटो में टाइगर पटौदी नेहरू जी के बगल में बैठे दिख रहे हैं।

सोहा ने कैप्शन में लिखा कि उनके माता-पिता के भी बड़े सपने थे जो कड़ी मेहनत से पूरे हुए। उन्होंने यह भी बताया कि नेहरू जी अपना जन्मदिन बच्चों के नाम करना चाहते थे ताकि हर बच्चा बड़े सपने देख सके। 💭

बता दें कि शर्मिला और टाइगर पटौदी 1965 में मिले थे और 1968 में दोनों की शादी हुई थी। उनके तीन बच्चे सैफ, सबा और सोहा हैं।

क्या आपने पटौदी फैमिली की ये ऐतिहासिक थ्रोबैक तस्वीरें देखीं? आपको सोहा का यह पोस्ट कैसा लगा, कमेंट्स में बताइए! 👇

ctx.title: Soha Ali Khan digs out childhood pictures of parents Sharmila Tagore, Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi with Nehru on Children's Day
ctx.summary: Children's Day is celebrated on November 14 every year to mark the birth anniversary of India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.
ctx.text:
Every year on November 14, Children’s Day is celebrated to mark the birth anniversary of India’s first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru. On the day, actor Soha Ali Khan took to her Instagram to post childhood pictures of her mom, actor Sharmila Tagore, and dad, cricketer Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi, aka Tiger Pataudi, with Nehru. She remarked on the significance of the occasion in her caption.
Soha posted three monochrome pictures on her Instagram account. One picture shows a young Sharmila pinning something onto Nehru’s coat. Another picture shows her standing beside him at the All India Radio (AIR). The third picture she posted shows Tiger sitting next to Nehru during an unknown occasion.
“Before they were my parents, they were children too. Today, on Children’s Day, which marks the birth anniversary of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, I’m sharing two special glimpses from our family albums,” wrote Soha in her caption, adding, “My mother as a little girl, my father as a boy, alongside a man who believed that children were the future of the nation.”
Soha further wrote about how Nehru’s birthday turned into Children’s Day, adding, “Pandit Nehru ji's birthday became Children’s Day in India because he didn't want the day to be about himself - he wanted to celebrate the future of the nation, our children and to give each of them an opportunity to dream big.”
She ended her note with a wish for all the children of the country, writing, “My parents had big dreams - with talent, hard work. perseverance and opportunity their dreams came true. May every child have the same chance turn their dreams into reality. Happy Children’s Day!”
Sharmila and Tiger met at an after-match party in 1965 and dated for about four years, during which he would woo her with everything from roses to air conditioners. They even lived together before their wedding in 1968. In June this year, Sharmila, while speaking to Barkha Dutt, recalled that everyone was sceptical about their relationship. “ Yash Chopra told me, 'These Nawabs are very doubtful people, so you have to be very careful.' He was a good friend and genuinely concerned,” she said.
On Siddharth Kannan’s show, Sharmila’s eldest daughter, Saba Ali Khan Pataudi, revealed that her mother had converted to Islam for the marriage, as was the norm at the time. Their three children, Saif Ali Khan, Saba and Soha, were born in 1970, 1976 and 1978 respectively. Tiger died at the age of 70 in 2011.
